A Snapshot of Your Day 

You start the day by reviewing portfolio-level progress across substation and grid monitoring products, gaining an overview of roadmap delivery, key risks, and interdependencies across regions and asset classes.

You meet with Product Managers to review product roadmaps, customer priorities, and execution status, ensuring alignment with the overall portfolio direction and business objectives. You work with R&D and engineering leaders to address major technical or capacity constraints and to ensure investments are focused on the most strategic initiatives.

In the afternoon, you focus on portfolio planning and steering: shaping the integrated portfolio roadmap, prioritizing initiatives across products, making investment trade-offs, and aligning with regional, commercial, and service organizations. You end the day advancing the long-term portfolio strategy for how Siemens Energy enables smarter, more resilient grid operations through monitoring, analytics, and digitalization.

How You’ll Make An Impact

Lead the Substation & Grid Monitoring portfolio, defining and owning the portfolio strategy and roadmap across asset classes, while driving prioritization and strategic trade offs to maximize customer value and business impact. 
Govern product strategy and roadmaps, providing oversight and challenge to ensure alignment with portfolio priorities, business objectives, and coherent execution across all products. 
Own the Health & Analytics Center (HAC) portfolio vision, setting strategic objectives, investment focus, and success criteria, while ensuring consistent translation into end to end product strategies and roadmaps. 
Shape the Digital Substation portfolio direction, defining priorities across monitoring, protection, control, and analytics, and ensuring cross product and cross unit alignment at portfolio level. 
Drive portfolio integration and cross functional alignment, resolving prioritization and dependency conflicts, setting portfolio guardrails, and ensuring clarity across regions, product lines, and adjacent portfolios. 
Hold portfolio level financial and organizational accountability, including R&D, CAPEX and OPEX planning, budget allocation, leadership and development of Product Management and Engineering functions, and external representation with customers, partners, and industry forums.


What You Bring

Completed university degree in electrical engineering or energy technology.
Strong product management and portfolio leadership experience in grid digitalization, substation automation with a proven ability to define product vision, portfolio strategy, and investment priorities across digital and physical grid domains.
Deep domain, technology, and digital understanding of grid digitalization concepts, protection & control systems, condition monitoring technologies, inspection data integration with strong software development foundations and machine learning analytics expertise as a distinct advantage, enabling informed portfolio-level strategic decisions grounded in technical and operational reality.
Demonstrated ability to lead and govern complex product portfolios, including responsibility for significant R&D budgets, CAPEX, and OPEX, and the capability to drive clear prioritization and investment trade-offs across grid digitalization initiatives and products.
Proven capability to translate customer needs, grid operational challenges, and market trends into differentiated product and portfolio strategies, working closely with Product Managers and Engineering teams to ensure effective translation into product strategies, roadmaps, and delivery outcomes.
Strong technical and business communication skills, with the ability to engage credibly with customers, engineering teams, and senior stakeholders on grid digitalization strategy, product direction, and technology-enabled business value.
Collaborative yet decisive leadership style, suited to cross-functional, multi-disciplinary environments, with a demonstrated ability to align Product Management and Engineering teams around portfolio strategy, while maintaining clear ownership and accountability.


About The Team

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical


We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

HighLevel’s Commerce platform is the system of record for how our customers sell — what they offer and how it is priced, how orders get fulfilled, and how money moves: payments in, invoices out, and books that balance . It spans product information, pricing, taxes, and channels; fulfillment and inventory; and the full finance stack of payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger — together powering commerce for a global base of agencies and businesses operating at scale.

We are seeking a Group Product Manager, Commerce , to lead product across three connected verticals — Business Operations, Fulfillment Operations, and Finance — and the team of Product Managers who own them. Deliver Finance – Own the payments, checkout, invoicing, and ledger/accounting roadmap, ensuring money moves securely and the books balance across providers and external systems like QuickBooks and Xero.

Own Outcomes & Metrics – Drive measurable growth in GMV, transaction success, merchant adoption, and reliability , using data to prioritize across a large and competing set of bets.

Partner with Senior Stakeholders – Work closely with engineering, design, finance, operations, and leadership to align on strategy, resourcing, and trade-offs, and represent Commerce in company-level planning.

Balance Delivery & Long-Term Bets – Keep near-term charters shipping on time while investing in the platform foundations that compound over the next several years .

Raise the Operating Bar – Establish the rituals, specs, and quality standards — discovery, prioritization, launch, and review — that make the team predictable, fast, and outcome-driven .

Experienced People Leader – You have managed and grown Product Managers, and you get energy from multiplying your impact through a strong, well-run team .

Platform & Commerce Depth – You have led product across commerce, payments, fintech, or a comparable transaction-heavy platform , and understand how catalog, fulfillment, and finance fit together.

Strategic and Execution-Focused – You can define a multi-vertical strategy and still hold your teams to crisp execution , ensuring ideas translate into shipped, measurable impact.

Systems Thinker – You see the interdependencies across modules and design for coherence, reuse, and shared contracts rather than one-off solutions.

Outcome- & Customer-Centric – You balance business goals, risk, and trust, keeping the merchants who run their business on the platform at the center of every decision.

Highly Data-Driven in Ambiguity – You are comfortable prioritizing across a broad, messy portfolio, using data to make sharp trade-offs without waiting for perfect information.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of Product Management experience , including 2+ years directly managing Product Managers , and 10+ years of total professional experience.

About HighLevel

About us
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our people
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts

Role Overview

HighLevel processes payments at significant scale for the businesses that run on our platform and yet only a fraction of the businesses we serve have adopted payments at all. The constraint is structural rather than one of awareness: adoption is decided by the agencies who serve these businesses, and they have never had a commercial reason to act. We are hiring a Senior Product Manager - Commerce Growth to close that gap and make payments adoption the fastest-compounding line in our Commerce business.

This role owns the adoption and monetisation charter for Commerce end to end. It spans partner incentive design, the growth mechanics that move a business from signing up to transacting consistently, the partner-facing surfaces those programmes live in, and the commercial model underneath them. It is a general-management role as much as a product one, you will own the unit economics, the programme budget, and the evidence that the investment is working.

This role is ideal for product managers who have built growth or partner programmes at scale, who are comfortable being measured on a commercial outcome rather than a feature list, and who bring the analytical rigour to distinguish growth that was genuinely caused from growth that would have happened anyway.

What You'll Do

Own the payments adoption charter end to end - the strategy, roadmap and operating plan that take adoption and transacting volume to a multiple of today's levels, and the commercial targets attached to them.

Design, launch and iterate partner incentive programmes that make adoption commercially compelling for the agencies who drive it including eligibility models, qualification logic, payout mechanics and the controls that keep the programmes durable and abuse-resistant.

Own the partner-facing product surfaces where these programmes are discovered, understood and acted on progress, earnings and next-best-action, designed to scale to tens of thousands of partners without manual support.

Own the unit economics: customer acquisition cost, payback period, contribution margin and programme budget - modelled, forecast, and defensible to Finance and leadership.

Build a disciplined experimentation practice - randomised tests, holdout groups and incrementality measurement so that pricing and programme decisions are evidence-led rather than intuition-led.

Apply growth-hacking rigour across the adoption funnel: segmentation, lifecycle triggers, in-product prompts and targeted campaigns, in partnership with Lifecycle Marketing, Community and Support.

Lead commercial conversations with our largest agency partners, where bespoke arrangements rather than self-serve programmes are what move the number.

Own the monthly performance narrative - adoption, retention, cost efficiency and programme health and the decision to scale, hold or retire each initiative.

Partner with Analytics, Finance, Risk and Commerce platform engineering on the measurement, controls and infrastructure the charter depends on.

What Success Looks Like

Payments adoption grows at a multiple of its current rate, with the uplift demonstrably attributable to the work rather than to underlying trend

Incentive investment pays back inside its target window, measured on contribution rather than headline revenue

Partners understand what they have earned and why, without needing to contact support

Programme abuse remains negligible and is contained by automated controls rather than manual review

Programme spend tracks forecast, with variance understood and explained

Minimum Qualifications

8–10 years of product management experience

Experience owning a growth, partner, referral or incentive programme where the commercial mechanic itself was the product

Comfort owning a commercial outcome end to end acquisition cost, payback, contribution margin and defending it to a finance audience

A track record of running controlled experiments and drawing the right conclusion from them, including the unwelcome one

Experience with payments, fintech, marketplaces or another business where unit economics are the product strategy

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in partner, reseller or franchise ecosystems where a third party not the end user makes the adoption decision

Familiarity with payment economics: processing rates, take rate, volume tiers, and how payment method mix affects platform monetisation

Experience designing abuse and fraud controls for a rewards, referral or affiliate programme

Background in vertical SaaS or platform businesses that monetise payments alongside subscriptions

Who This Role Is For

Product managers who think in unit economics, and who will hold the line when an initiative is popular but does not pay for itself.

PMs who treat commercial programmes as product surfaces with an interface, a rulebook and a feedback loop rather than a spreadsheet handed to marketing.

People energised by a very specific problem: getting tens of thousands of independent businesses to act on your behalf, repeatedly, at a price that makes sense.

Why Should You Join Us?

At HighLevel, we foster an exciting and dynamic work environment driven by a passionate team. We believe in a collective responsibility where no task is considered someone else's job. Our unwavering focus is on providing value to our users, and we achieve this by delivering solutions swiftly through lean principles, allowing us to bring products to market in a matter of weeks rather than quarters. Every good idea is put to the test, ensuring that we maintain a high standard of innovation. We prioritise the well-being of our team, recognizing that by taking care of them, they can better serve our users. We embrace the concept of continuous and iterative improvement, understanding that progress is an ongoing journey. We are also a well funded & profitable company.

Join us at HighLevel, and you will have the opportunity to learn the intricacies of scaling a B2B SaaS startup and develop impactful products that cater to the needs of our customers.

Identify and prioritize automation use cases with the highest customer impact, grounded in field data, customer interviews, and win/loss analysis.

Partner with GTM, Customer Success, and Sales to develop positioning, enablement materials, and go-to-market strategies that communicate the business value of DEX and automation capabilities to economic buyers (CIOs, DEX Program Owners).

Job Description

This is a remote position.

Experience Level

We're looking for a seasoned Product Owner with at least 2–4 years of experience owning a product backlog end-to-end within an Agile delivery environment. You should be a "delivery craftsperson" who can demonstrate a track record of turning ambiguous, cross-team requirements into shipped, working software — with particular comfort operating inside platforms where your product's success depends on coordination with teams you don't manage.

Role Overview

As a Product Owner, you will own the backlog and delivery cadence for one product within a tightly interconnected platform, where your product's roadmap depends on — and feeds into — several sibling products. You'll act as the point of alignment between engineering teams, supporting product managers, and client stakeholders, translating business and compliance needs into backlog items ready for a development team to execute against.

A key part of the role is holding the line on requirements quality: defining clear acceptance criteria before work enters a sprint, and sequencing competing demands — new features, maintenance of live services, and production support — that your team carries simultaneously. Because your product does not operate in isolation, a large part of the job is coordinating dependencies across teams that don't report to you.

Key Responsibilities

Backlog Ownership & Requirements Definition: Own and prioritize the product backlog; define acceptance criteria for accuracy, completeness, and readiness before stories are marked sprint-ready.
Cross-Team Dependency Coordination: Sequence and negotiate delivery across multiple dependent engineering teams (platform, integration, infrastructure, and adjacent product teams), since most features require multi-team scheduling rather than single-team execution.
Delivery Prioritization Under Competing Demands: Balance new feature development, maintenance of live production services, and active production support within the same backlog, without letting one silently starve the others.
Domain Ramp-Up: Build working depth in the specific technical and regulatory domain tied to your assigned product — this may include healthcare EDI transaction standards, web-automation/data-extraction reliability, credential and access-security models, or regulated payments and remittance processing, depending on placement.
Stakeholder & Requirements Governance: Partner with the supporting Product Manager and client-side stakeholders to close open requirement decisions before development starts, hold sign-off discipline, and manage rework risk from late-stage scope changes.
Data & Interface Quality Ownership: Where your product's output feeds downstream systems, own the interface contract (field definitions, data completeness, naming) to prevent avoidable rework further down the chain.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

Proven Product Ownership Experience: Track record owning a backlog end-to-end in an Agile environment, ideally within a platform where products are tightly coupled rather than independent.
Domain Adaptability: Comfort ramping quickly into unfamiliar technical or regulatory domains — some assignments require near-immediate fluency (e.g., regulated payments, EDI standards), while others allow for a longer runway.
Cross-Functional Coordination Skills: Demonstrated ability to sequence work and resolve competing priorities across multiple engineering teams that don't report into the same chain.
Analytical Rigor: Ability to write precise, testable acceptance criteria and reason through data quality or completeness gaps before they become delivery blockers.
Strong Stakeholder Communication: Comfortable representing product status and trade-offs to both engineering teams and client-facing stakeholders, in plain, non-technical language when needed.
Judgment Under Ambiguity: Able to recognize when a decision needs escalation versus independent ownership — particularly important for the more regulation-heavy assignments, where working without senior support isn't advisable early on.

The Ideal Candidate

Director of Product
AI Cloud and Orchestration, Velocis Platform
Reports to Chief Product Officer
Location Mumbai
Function Product Leadership, AI Infrastructure (Velocis)

Why this role, why now?
Neysa is building the AI cloud for the era where AI runs in production rather than in pilots. The promise we are claiming to deliver is operational confidence, the ability for an enterprise to run AI predictably, affordably and accountably. Infrastructure choices now decide which AI programmes are viable at all, and for us sovereignty means strategic control rather than a compliance checkbox.
Velocis is how we deliver that, across GPU as a service and our AI platform as a service. We are scaling from strong early proof into a platform that serves sovereign enterprise buyers in India and large offtake capacity globally. This role exists to help set product direction and to make it real.

The Role
We are hiring a Senior Director of Product to sit alongside the Chief Product Officer as a balanced strategist and operator, and to co-own the Velocis product ecosystem. You will help shape the two-year product strategy and you will own the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off that turn it into shipped platform. Engineering, infrastructure operations, design and go-to-market are your delivery partners, and product holds the pen on what gets built and in what order.
You will move between whiteboarding high-density cluster architecture with an executive buyer in one hour and running a deep specification review with a product manager in the next. Both are the job.

What you will own?Product strategy and roadmap
• Co-own the 12 and 24 month strategy for Velocis across GPU as a service and the AI platform, and hold the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off end to end.
• Ship the Velocis AI platform stack and move straight into post-launch feature velocity, reliability, and the Day-0 and Day-1 user journey.
• Keep a live read on the global AI infrastructure landscape, across orchestration layers, sovereign cloud, inference economics and power and density, so Velocis holds its edge.

Team and craft
• Lead, mentor and hold accountable a team of four or more product managers across the core Velocis modules.
• Build a product culture of extreme ownership, technical precision and fast feedback, and raise the hiring bar as the team grows.
• Coach high-potential talent and step in where a track needs lift.
Enterprise commercials and offtake
• Partner with the CPO and CEO on offtake opportunities from 1,000 to 8,000 GPUs, shaping orchestration specs, tenant isolation and SLA commitments.
• Act as executive product sponsor for key Indian enterprise accounts.
• Turn bespoke offtake and enterprise requirements into platform capabilities the wider base can use, without fragmenting the core codebase. This is one of the hardest and most important parts of the role.
Platform economics
• Own core product economics with the CPO, across GPU utilisation efficiency, gross margin, tenant density and feature monetisation.
• Treat onboarding time to value and expansion as first-order outcomes, since Velocis revenue behaves as consumption rather than subscription and expansion is the dominant growth lever.

What you bring?
• Ten or more years in product management, with four or more leading product teams. Hands-on experience in GPU computing, AI or ML orchestration or HPC is ideal, and strong candidates from adjacent large-scale cloud or general-purpose cloud infrastructure, with the ability to ramp fast, will be considered.
• A track record of shipping complex B2B infrastructure products from concept to meaningful revenue scale.
• Fluency across GPU infrastructure on NVIDIA and AMD, container and workload orchestration such as Kubernetes, Slurm and Ray, VPC and network topologies, object storage and dedicated inference pipelines.
• Working command of multi-tenancy and tenant isolation, observability and cost attribution, sovereign deployment patterns such as air-gapped clusters and customer-managed keys, and inference economics measured as cost per token and P99 latency.
• Commercial fluency, so that you connect product decisions to gross margin, resource efficiency and customer return.

How you work?
• You zoom out to market positioning and a two-year horizon, and zoom in to specifications, telemetry and the granular detail, without losing either.
• You have a default to action and high standards, and you pair them with the judgment to say no and to sequence well.
• You are a low-ego and articulate communicator who earns credibility quickly with engineers, enterprise CTOs and executive leadership.
• You are comfortable building in a category that is still being created.

Your first 90 days
• Take full ownership of the roadmap and prioritisation across the PM tracks, with clear ownership lines in place.
• Land the near-term Velocis milestones with clean telemetry on adoption and stability.
• Establish a working rhythm with engineering, operations and go-to-market that delivers predictably.

Success in the first 6 to 12 months
• Roadmap predictability and release velocity, with the Velocis milestones shipped and instrumented for adoption and reliability.
• Movement on the economics you own, across GPU utilisation efficiency, gross margin and tenant density.
• Time to production for offtake customers and time to value in onboarding, both trending down.
• Expansion on named enterprise and offtake accounts.
• A high-functioning product team with clear ownership and a rising bar.

The Product Owner partners closely with Business stakeholders, Data Engineering, BI/Reporting, Data Science, Governance, and Platform teams to ensure data products are reliable, intuitive, scalable, and aligned with Kroll’s strategic priorities. The role emphasizes clarity of ownership, predictable delivery, and measurable business impact in a complex, enterprise data environment.

Key Responsibilities

Product Ownership & Accountability

Define and own the product vision, roadmap, and backlog for enterprise data, analytics, or AI product areas.
Serve as the single point of accountability for product outcomes, delivery health, and user experience.
Define and communicate product goals, success metrics, and value drivers to stakeholders and delivery teams.
Ensure products operate with clear ownership, release discipline, and lifecycle management, behaving like true products—not one‑off projects.

Stakeholder Engagement & Business Alignment

Act as the primary interface between the CDO and business, finance, and functional leaders for assigned domains.
Partner with stakeholders to prioritize demand, manage tradeoffs, and align delivery to business timelines.
Translate business needs into clear, actionable requirements without compromising data integrity or architectural standards.
Establish and maintain trusted relationships that enable fast decision‑making and alignment.

Backlog, Roadmap & Delivery Management

Own and maintain a prioritized, well‑defined backlog with clear acceptance criteria and readiness standards.
Work with Program Managers, Scrum Masters, and delivery teams to plan releases and manage dependencies.
Balance short‑term delivery needs with long‑term product health, scalability, and maintainability.
Surface risks, constraints, or scope trade‑offs early to enable leadership decisions.

Governance, Quality & Standards

Partner with Data Governance, Data Stewards, and Platform Owners to ensure:
Consistent KPI definitions and metric logic
Data quality, lineage, and trust standards
Alignment with enterprise data architecture and security policies
Ensure products meet operational readiness standards prior to release and are supported post‑launch.
Adoption, Value & Continuous Improvement

Drive product adoption by ensuring solutions is intuitive, reliable, and aligned to real user workflows.
Define and track usage, adoption, and value realization metrics.
Collect feedback and iterate to continuously improve product experience and impact.
Support leadership by providing a clear narrative on what is delivered, what value it creates, and what comes next.

Alation is pioneering the next era of data intelligence - powered by AI agents and trusted data. Organizations around the world rely on Alation to drive self-service analytics, cloud transformation, data governance, and AI innovation. Our technology helps enterprises connect people and data to make faster, smarter, and more confident decisions. With more than $340M in funding - valued at over $1.7 billion and more than 650 customers, including 40% of the Fortune 100.
As data becomes the foundation of every business, Alation is leading the way in helping organizations unlock their full potential. By bringing intelligence, automation, and trust to every interaction, we empower customers to scale data-driven innovation with confidence and speed.
Joining Alation means being part of a winning team shaping the future of AI-powered data intelligence. We move fast, think big, and deliver results together.
About Alation
Alation is the creator of AIOS - the intelligence operating system for enterprises that cannot afford to get AI wrong. When software breaks, it throws an error. When an AI agent breaks, it produces a confident, wrong answer - and most organizations have no system to catch it before that answer drives a decision. AIOS keeps data, context, and agents in sync in one open, governed, self-improving system, so every decision an agent makes holds up.
Having pioneered the data catalog market, Alation is trusted by over 600 enterprises worldwide - including 40% of the Fortune 500 - to power their most critical data and AI initiatives. The problems we tackle are complex, high-impact, and deeply technical. This is not a slow-moving environment. We build fast, ship real things, learn from customers, and iterate relentlessly.
About the Role
AIOS doesnt work without connectivity. Agents fail when bad data reaches them, when context is stale, or when the environment shifts underneath them - and the defense against all three starts with rich, current metadata flowing in from the systems where enterprise data actually lives. Connectors are how AIOS sees the enterprise. Thats this teams job, and its getting harder and more interesting as the data and AI landscape shifts under everyones feet.
Were looking for a Senior Product Manager to own this problem end to end. Youll inherit a portfolio of 80+ integrations spanning the modern and legacy data stack, and a mandate to define what connectivity means in an agentic world - new systems, new types of sources (including the agents and AI tools that are themselves becoming metadata sources), new extraction techniques, and AI applied wherever it genuinely moves the needle.
This is a senior IC role with real scope. You wont be handed a polished roadmap or mature systems - youll sharpen the strategy, make the calls, and ship. This is a role for builders.
What Youll Do
  • Own the Connector mission: make it fast and easy for customers to bring rich, valuable metadata into AIOS
  • Drive the strategy for 80+ existing integrations - what to deepen, what to optimize, what to sunset
  • Lead expansion into new systems and entirely new categories of data sources as the AI landscape reshapes what "a data source" means
  • Turn ambiguous problems into clear direction, scoped bets, and shipped solutions
  • Talk to customers constantly - validate direction, pressure-test ideas, iterate fast
  • Work directly with engineering to define requirements, reason through tradeoffs, and move quickly
  • Apply AI strategically across the connector portfolio - both in the product and in how you work
  • Raise the bar on how we build, not just what we build
Who This Role Is For
We care more about how you operate than where youve been. Traits and trajectory matter to us more than a checklist of domain credentials.
You might be a great fit if you:
  • Are gritty and resilient - you dont stall when things are unclear or hard
  • Have a strong sense of ownership - you feel accountable for outcomes, not just tasks
  • Are deeply curious - you ask why, dig into systems, and want to understand how things really work
  • Are AI-native by instinct - you already use AI tools daily to think, write, analyze, and prototype, and you actively push the people around you to work differently
  • Thrive in fast-moving, high-expectation environments
  • Love building, especially in under-defined or shifting problem spaces
  • Make decisions with incomplete information and adjust quickly
  • Communicate clearly and align engineers, designers, and stakeholders around a direction
Experience Skills
  • 5+ years in product management, engineering, or similar problem-solving roles - but we weight demonstrated traits and trajectory over years served
  • A track record of shipping real products or systems that customers used and cared about
  • Strong analytical thinking and comfort operating in complex, technical domains
  • Sharp written communication - PRDs, specs, narratives, decision docs

  • Preferred (not required): experience with enterprise data environments, data integration, metadata management, or developer-facing products

GURGAON, IN, 122001

At McCormick, we bring our passion for flavor to work each day. We encourage growth, respect everyone's contributions and do what's right for our business, our people, our communities and our planet. Join us on our quest to make every meal and moment better.

Founded in Baltimore, MD in 1889 in a room and a cellar by 25-year-old Willoughby McCormick with three employees, McCormick is a global leader in flavour. With over 14,000 employees around the world and more than $6 Billion in annual sales, the Company manufactures, markets, and distributes spices, seasoning mixes, condiments and other flavourful products to the entire food industry, retail outlets, food manufactures, food service businesses and consumers.

While our global headquarters are in the Baltimore, Maryland, USA area, McCormick operates and serves customers from nearly 60 locations in 25 countries and 170 markets in Asia-Pacific, China, Europe, Middle East and Africa, and the Americas, including North, South and Central America

Position Overview

The Data Product Manager (SAP Analytics) leads the strategy, design, and delivery of trusted, high-value data products for McCormick’s SAP Analytics. This role is accountable for the end-to-end lifecycle, quality, and adoption of SAP Analytics data products that enable measurable business outcomes — including strategic decision-making, performance transparency, and operational excellence across McCormick.

The Data Product Manager (SAP Analytics) is accountable for the definition, championing, and most importantly, delivery of trusted, high-value data products. The role works as one with McCormick’s Transformation & Technology (including Data & Analytics, Data Governance, Information Security and Technology teams) and Global Business Solutions (including Automation and Data Science & Engineering teams) functions to connect people, platforms, and processes — establishing a trusted, intelligent, and connected SAP Analytics data foundation that supports McCormick’s global growth and enterprise value creation.

Key Responsibilities

Description

Data Product Strategy & Vision: Defines the strategy and roadmap for SAP Analytics data products that enable functional priorities and deliver measurable business value in alignment with McCormick’s enterprise data strategies—both at the functional level, as established by the Data Owner, and at the enterprise level as established by the Chief Data & Analytics Officer (CDAO). Partners with stakeholders and Transformation & Technology Business Relationship Managers (BRMs) to prioritize initiatives based on business impact, ROI potential, and readiness for advanced analytics and AI applications. Directs the design and delivery of data products that generate tangible business outcomes while ensuring scalability, interoperability, and long‑term sustainability. Establishes and maintains strong cross‑functional alignment to effectively prioritize initiatives, communicate progress, and advance McCormick’s data‑driven transformation.

Data Product Lifecycle Ownership: Directs the planning, prioritization, and delivery of SAP Analytic data products through an agile, iterative approach that ensures responsiveness to evolving business needs. Manages the data product backlog—translating functional requirements into clear, actionable user stories—and directs Data Engineers, Data Architects (who are part of the AI and analytics product teams), and Data Stewards to deliver high-quality, secure, and accessible data solutions. Oversees release planning and approval in alignment with governance and quality standards.

Data Quality, Trust & Compliance: Drives adherence to enterprise and functional standards for data quality, lineage, metadata, and compliance across SAP Analytic data products. Partners with key stakeholders to embed governance and regulatory requirements into data product design and delivery. Monitors data quality and trust metrics, driving continuous improvement to ensure data products remain reliable, reusable, and fit for analytical and AI-driven use cases.

Data Enablement & Workforce Readiness: Enables relevant stakeholders to easily find, understand, and use trusted data by ensuring data products are well-documented, cataloged, and supported with clear usage guidance. Partners with key stakeholders to maintain accurate catalog entries, metadata, and reference materials that promote consistent and compliant data use. Leads initiatives to strengthen engagement with data products and activate a culture where data is valued, trusted, and responsibly used as “ground truth”.

Data Product Performance & Value Realization: Defines and tracks performance metrics to measure the adoption, quality, and business impact of SAP Analytic data products. Establishes feedback loops that leverage usage insights and stakeholder input to drive continuous improvement and optimization. Partners with the Data Owner to quantify and communicate data product value, demonstrating significant advancement McCormick’s digital and AI transformation.

Required Qualifications

Level of Education and Discipline

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business Analytics, or other applicable field
Candidates with strong SAP Analytics qualifications and a demonstrated track record of data literacy may also be considered in lieu of the above degree requirements

Experience - functional/industry/commercial knowledge, business acumen

15+ years of experience in data product management, data strategy, or data governance within a complex or global organization
12+ years of experience in SAP Analytics within the CPG, food, or manufacturing industries
Proven ability to manage the end-to-end lifecycle of data products, from vision and roadmap through delivery and adoption
Strong understanding of data architecture, quality, metadata, and governance, with the ability to connect technical design to business value and apply modern data product concepts (e.g. data mesh)
Demonstrated success working in Agile environments, collaborating with cross-functional teams including Data Engineering, IT, and business stakeholders
Solid business acumen and communication skills, with experience quantifying data product value and driving data adoption across functions

Interpersonal Skills - leadership, interactions, communication, influence

Strategic thinking skills are essential to develop data products that create business value and support key business objectives and strategies. By connecting business context with technical execution, the role balances competing needs, prioritizes product backlogs, and ensures successful delivery of data products that achieve business objectives while driving accountability for data quality, governance, and adoption within an Agile, iterative environment.

Influencing and collaboration skills are critical to align diverse stakeholders and advance McCormick’s enterprise data and governance strategy. The Data Product Owner builds trusted relationships across multiple functions including RDQR, Transformation & Technology, and Global Business Solutions, leading through influence and collaboration to deliver data products that meet evolving business needs.

Communication skills are required to articulate data product vision, value, and progress in a clear and compelling way. The role tailors messages to different audiences, ensuring complex ideas are conveyed with clarity and purpose. Active listening, transparency, and structured communication are used to align expectations, secure engagement, and reinforce accountability for trusted, high‑value data products.

At McCormick, we have over a 100-year legacy based on our “Power of People” principle. This principle fosters an unusually dedicated workforce requiring a culture of respect, recognition, inclusion and collaboration based on the highest ethical value

WHY WOR
